This Petition, Coming On For Final Hearing, This
Day, Order Was Made Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs Justice M G Uma
 Oral Order
(Per: Hon'Ble Mrs Justice M G Uma) The petitioner herein being respondent No.1 in
Crl.Misc.No.512/2015 on the file of the learned Senior Civil Judge and Jmfc, Basavakalyan [for
short, 'the Trial Court'] is impugning the order dated 28.10.2021 allowing Crl.Misc.No.512/2015 in
part against the petitioner herein and directing him to pay monthly maintenance of Nc:
2025:Khc-K:5224 Hc-Kar Rs.5,000/- from the date of order, which was modified in Criminal
Appeal No.5025/2022 on the file of the learned II-Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bidar
sitting at Basavakalyan [for short, 'the First Appellate Court'] vide judgment dated 10.10.2022,
wherein the First Appellate Court dismissed the appeal and has ordered the petitioner herein to pay
monthly maintenance of Rs.5,000/- to the respondent herein from the date of petition i.e.,
01.01.2015 till her remarriage or death.

2. Facts of the case in brief are that the respondent herein as petitioner filed Crl.Misc.No.512/2015
before the Trial Court against the present petitioner alleging that, he is her husband, and respondent
Nos.2 and 3 are her parents-in-law.

She filed the petition under Section 12 of the Protection of
Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 [for short, 'the D.V. Act'] claiming protection order
under Section 18, resident order under Section 19, maintenance of Rs.20,000/- per month under
Sunilkumar S/O Subhash Bolsure vs Roopa Claims As W/O Sunil Bolsure on 8 September, 2025

Section 20, compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- under Section Nc: 2025:Khc-K:5224 Hc-Kar 22 of
D.V. Act.

The Trial Court, while allowing the petition in part, awarded monthly maintenance of
Rs.5,000/- against the petitioner herein while rejecting the claim against his parents and also the
reliefs claimed under Sections 18, 19 and 22 of D.V. Act.

Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioner
herein has preferred Criminal Appeal No.5025/2022.

The First Appellate Court, on re- appreciation
of the materials on record, dismissed the appeal by confirming the order passed by the Trial Court.
Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioner is before this Court.

3. Heard Smt. Vijaya M. Patil, learned counsel for the petitioner and Smt. Vidya S. Totad, learned
counsel for the respondent.
Perused the materials on record, including the Trial Court records.

4. In view of the rival contentions urged by learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would
arise for my consideration is:
Nc: 2025:Khc-K:5224 Hc-Kar "Whether the revision petitioner has made out any
ground to interfere with the impugned order passed by the Trial Court, which was
confirmed by the First Appellate Court?"

My answer to the above point is in the 'Affirmative' for the following reasons:
Reasons
5.

It is the contention of the respondent herein that, she is the legally wedded wife of the petitioner
herein.

She was subjected to cruelty by the petitioner and she was ousted from the matrimonial
house.
In the meantime, she had begotten a son by the name Sidharth.

It is pertinent to note that,
the respondent has examined herself as Pw.1, got examined Pw.2 and Pw.3 and got marked Exs.P1
to P18 in support of her contention.

While the petitioner herein as respondent before the Trial Court
examined Rw.1 to Rw.3 and got marked Exs.R1 to R20 in support of his contention.

The
cross-examination of Pw.1 to Pw.3 discloses that, the petitioner herein has denied his Nc:
2025:Khc-K:5224 Hc-Kar relationship with the respondent.

Accordingly, the respondent has
examined himself as Rw.1.

Even he was subjected to cross-examination, and except suggesting the
contention taken by the petitioner and getting denial, nothing has been elicited from him to
disbelieve his version.
6. The respondent herein who is examined as Pw.1 was subjected to cross-examination where she
admitted

that, her sister Priyanka had married one Sanjukumar but denied the suggestion that she
also married said Sanjukumar

. She denied the suggestion that, there is no relationship between her
and the petitioner herein.

During further chief examination, Ex.P15 was marked on behalf of the
respondent herein to contend that, said Sanjukumar has already divorced her.

This document
supports the contention by the respondent before the Trial Court that she had married Sanjukumar
and therefore, she is his wife..

Nc: 2025:Khc-K:5224 Hc-Kar
Sunilkumar S/O Subhash Bolsure vs Roopa Claims As W/O
Sunil Bolsure on 8 September, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94594761/
3

7.

The respondent herein has got marked Exs.P16 to P18 to contend that, she had begotten a son in
the marriage with the petitioner herein.

As per the averments made in the petition, she has married
the petitioner herein on 02.09.2014 and later she was ousted from the matrimonial house on
21.11.2014.

She had filed a criminal complaint registered in Crime No.134/2014 of Basavakalyan
Rural police station against the petitioner and his parents on 21.11.2014 alleging commission of the
offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 read with Section 34 of Ipc.

Ex.P16 is the birth
certificate pertaining to the son of the respondent born in the wedlock with the petitioner herein,
but strangely date of birth of Sidharth was on 12.11.2020.

When it is the specific contention of the
respondent that, she was ousted from the matrimonial house during 2014, there is no explanation as
to how she has begotten a son from the petitioner during 2020

. 
8. It is also pertinent to note that, the petitioner herein has produced Ex.R16 - the order passed by
the Nc: 2025:Khc-K:5224 Hc-Kar Trial Court in C.C.No.39/2015, acquitting the petitioner herein
and his parents for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 504 read with Section 34 of Ipc.
Exs.R19 and R20 are the depositions by the parents of the petitioner herein, who have categorically
stated that, the respondent had married to one Sanjukumar, and later she had married to Anil.

Ex.P15 is the admitted document, according to which, Sunilkumar had issued the document as
'Bidugade Patra' to be the divorce letter to his wife.

Ex .P15 is not having any validity in the eye of
law.

When the materials on record discloses that, the respondent had married one Sanjukumar and
there is no decree of divorce between the respondent and her first husband Sanjukumar, the
contention of the respondent that, she is the legally wedded wife of the petitioner herein, cannot be
accepted.
9.

Learned counsel for the respondent contended that, the respondent and the petitioner were in
'live in relationship' and therefore, the petition before the Trial Nc: 2025:Khc-K:5224 Hc-Kar
Court was filed.

Unfortunately, no such contention was ever taken by the respondent herein before
the Trial Court either in the pleadings or in the evidence.
Under such circumstances, I am of the
opinion

that the respondent is not entitled for any relief as she has failed to prove her domestic
relationship with the petitioner at any point of time.
10. I have gone through the impugned order passed by the Trial Court in Crl.Misc.No.512/2015.

The
Court has proceeded to allow the petition very casually by observing that, the relationship between
the parties are admitted, and that itself proves that the respondent is the wife of the petitioner
herein.

The Court appears to have ignored all the materials on record, both oral and documentary,
and proceeded to allow the petition without assigning any valid reasons.

The First Appellate Court
in Criminal Appeal No.5025/2022 placed reliance on Exs.P1 to P10 - the marriage photos and
Ex.P15 - the divorce letter, to form an opinion that there was a valid marriage
- 10 -
Nc: 2025:Khc-K:5224 Hc-Kar between the petitioner and the respondent herein. It has also
placed reliance on Exs.P16 to P18, ignoring the specific pleadings in the petition that, the
respondent was ousted from the matrimonial house during 2014.

Therefore, I am of the opinion
that, the Trial Court as well as the First Appellate Court have committed grave error in passing the
Sunilkumar S/O Subhash Bolsure vs Roopa Claims As W/O Sunil Bolsure on 8 September, 2025

4

impugned orders ignoring the materials on record and hence, the same are liable to be set aside.

Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
Order
i) Criminal revision petition is allowed.

ii) The order dated 28.10.2021 passed in Crl.Misc.No.512/2015, on the file of learned
Senior Civil Judge and Additional Mact, Basavakalyan and the judgment da

ted 10.10.2022 passed in Criminal Appeal No.5025/2022 on the file of learned II Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bidar - 11 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:5224 HC-KAR sitting at Basavakalyan, modifying the order passed by the Trial Court, are hereby set aside.
